svg.title: 03_output_board.svg
svg.desc: Labelled rectangular devices, terminal names at every conductor end, and continuous wire paths. Design draft.

g.text: Mechanical relay contacts command Bosch coils; MOSFET board controls the remaining planned loads.
DESIGN DRAFT • TBD = terminal/pin or wire specification not yet verified • Repeated device labels refer to the same device.
Wire colors indicate function. Actual harness colors and AWG remain TBD unless explicitly printed.
F03 fuse sits upstream of this conductor; gauge/color TBD. Verify device terminal order.
Assign exact GPIO/interface terminals before installation; each line is a separate conductor.
Do not wire Pi GPIO directly to the OPMSD16 12V input version. Exact sinking/common circuit is still unresolved.
Map preserves existing schematic channel allocation, except Y07/Y15 are now spare after the mechanical-relay assignments. The I/O assignment plan now matches this
baseline; verify against final software/HAL before installation.
Map preserves existing schematic channel allocation, except Y07/Y15 are now spare after the mechanical-relay assignments. The I/O assignment plan now matches this
baseline; verify against final software/HAL before installation.
NC contacts unused. Outputs 5–8 spare. Physical board RLY-01 is not the same naming scope as channel RLY-01.
Verify 3.3V trigger compatibility and polarity; fit a suitable interface if required. The board contacts switch +12V to Bosch coils, not vehicle load current.
Remaining Y outputs and the 16-channel control interface are provisional. Software/HAL map must match the final physical terminals.
Direct MOSFET ceiling ≤4A continuous only after thermal/inrush verification. Every downstream load/coil needs its proper ground return.
Source: repository design docs, fuse schedule and hardware inventory. Pin order is not a physical PCB layout.
